title: CTS Evangelism — Unit 10: Follow-Up and Discipleship (Bilingual)

blocks.en: 📖 Evangelism — Unit 10: Follow-Up and Discipleship in Evangelism
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Evangelismo — Unidad 10: Seguimiento y Discipulado en el Evangelismo

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary · Dr. Wayne Cook, Author and Professor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Seminary Director
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala · Dr. Wayne Cook, Autor y Profesor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Director del Seminario

blocks.en: Orientation
blocks.es_reference: Orientación

blocks.en: Evangelism does not end with a response to the gospel. A common mistake is to treat evangelism as complete once a person has made a profession of faith. Scripture, however, presents evangelism as the beginning of a process that leads to discipleship. True conversion results in new life, and that life must be nurtured and developed. Follow-up is essential to help new believers grow in understanding, assurance, and obedience.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo no termina con una respuesta al evangelio. Un error común es tratar el evangelismo como completo una vez que una persona ha hecho una profesión de fe. Las Escrituras, sin embargo, presentan el evangelismo como el comienzo de un proceso que conduce al discipulado. La verdadera conversión resulta en una nueva vida, y esa vida debe ser nutrida y desarrollada. El seguimiento es esencial para ayudar a los nuevos creyentes a crecer en entendimiento, seguridad y obediencia.

blocks.en: I. The Biblical Mandate for Discipleship
blocks.es_reference: I. El Mandato Bíblico del Discipulado

blocks.en: Jesus did not command His followers merely to make converts, but to make disciples:
blocks.es_reference: Jesús no mandó a sus seguidores meramente a hacer conversos, sino a hacer discípulos:

blocks.en: "Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you." (Matthew 28:19–20, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Por tanto, id, y haced discípulos a todas las naciones, bautizándolos en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo; enseñándoles que guarden todas las cosas que os he mandado." (Mateo 28:19–20, RVG)

blocks.en: The goal of evangelism is not only a decision, but transformation. A disciple is a learner and a follower of Christ. To make disciples is to bring people not merely to a moment of profession but to a lifelong walk of obedience.
blocks.es_reference: La meta del evangelismo no es solo una decisión, sino la transformación. Un discípulo es un aprendiz y seguidor de Cristo. Hacer discípulos es llevar a las personas no meramente a un momento de profesión, sino a un caminar de obediencia de por vida.

blocks.en: II. The Evidence of Genuine Conversion
blocks.es_reference: II. La Evidencia de la Conversión Genuina

blocks.en: Not every profession of faith is evidence of true conversion. Jesus warned:
blocks.es_reference: No toda profesión de fe es evidencia de una verdadera conversión. Jesús advirtió:

blocks.en: "Not everyone who says to Me, 'Lord, Lord,' shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father in heaven." (Matthew 7:21, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "No todo el que me dice: Señor, Señor, entrará en el reino de los cielos, sino el que hace la voluntad de mi Padre que está en los cielos." (Mateo 7:21, RVG)

blocks.en: True conversion produces a changed heart, new desires, and spiritual growth. Follow-up helps discern whether a response is genuine, and gently establishes the new believer in the faith.
blocks.es_reference: La verdadera conversión produce un corazón cambiado, nuevos deseos y crecimiento espiritual. El seguimiento ayuda a discernir si una respuesta es genuina, y establece con gentileza al nuevo creyente en la fe.

blocks.en: III. The Importance of Immediate Follow-Up
blocks.es_reference: III. La Importancia del Seguimiento Inmediato

blocks.en: When a person responds to the gospel, immediate follow-up is critical. In Acts, new believers were quickly integrated into teaching and fellowship:
blocks.es_reference: Cuando una persona responde al evangelio, el seguimiento inmediato es crítico. En Hechos, los nuevos creyentes fueron integrados rápidamente a la enseñanza y la comunión:

blocks.en: "And they continued steadfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers." (Acts 2:42, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y perseveraban en la doctrina de los apóstoles, y en la comunión, y en el partimiento del pan, y en las oraciones." (Hechos 2:42, RVG)

blocks.en: Delay can lead to confusion, doubt, or discouragement. The early church did not leave new believers to themselves; it surrounded them with teaching and community from the very first days.
blocks.es_reference: La demora puede llevar a la confusión, la duda o el desánimo. La iglesia primitiva no dejó a los nuevos creyentes a su suerte; los rodeó de enseñanza y comunidad desde los primeros días.

blocks.en: IV. Teaching Foundational Truths
blocks.es_reference: IV. Enseñar las Verdades Fundamentales

blocks.en: New believers must be grounded in essential truths: assurance of salvation, the nature of God, the authority of Scripture, and the importance of prayer.
blocks.es_reference: Los nuevos creyentes deben ser cimentados en verdades esenciales: la seguridad de la salvación, la naturaleza de Dios, la autoridad de las Escrituras y la importancia de la oración.

blocks.en: "as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby." (1 Peter 2:2, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "desead, como niños recién nacidos, la leche espiritual no adulterada, para que por ella crezcáis." (1 Pedro 2:2, RVG)

blocks.en: Growth requires nourishment. A newborn left unfed will not thrive, and a new believer left untaught will struggle to grow.
blocks.es_reference: El crecimiento requiere alimento. Un recién nacido sin alimentar no prosperará, y un nuevo creyente sin enseñanza luchará por crecer.

blocks.en: V. The Role of the Church
blocks.es_reference: V. El Papel de la Iglesia

blocks.en: The church plays a central role in discipleship.
blocks.es_reference: La iglesia desempeña un papel central en el discipulado.

blocks.en: "And the Lord added to the church daily those who were being saved." (Acts 2:47, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y el Señor añadía cada día a la iglesia los que habían de ser salvos." (Hechos 2:47, RVG)

blocks.en: New believers need fellowship, teaching, and accountability. Discipleship is not meant to occur in isolation; it flourishes within the life of a healthy local church.
blocks.es_reference: Los nuevos creyentes necesitan comunión, enseñanza y rendición de cuentas. El discipulado no está destinado a ocurrir en aislamiento; florece dentro de la vida de una iglesia local sana.

blocks.en: VI. Encouraging Spiritual Growth
blocks.es_reference: VI. Fomentar el Crecimiento Espiritual

blocks.en: Spiritual growth involves reading Scripture, prayer, obedience, and fellowship. It is gradual but intentional.
blocks.es_reference: El crecimiento espiritual involucra la lectura de las Escrituras, la oración, la obediencia y la comunión. Es gradual pero intencional.

blocks.en: "but grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ." (2 Peter 3:18, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "mas creced en la gracia y el conocimiento de nuestro Señor y Salvador Jesucristo." (2 Pedro 3:18, RVG)

blocks.en: No one matures overnight. The believer who walks faithfully in these ordinary means of grace will, over time, be conformed more and more to Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Nadie madura de la noche a la mañana. El creyente que camina fielmente en estos medios ordinarios de gracia será, con el tiempo, conformado cada vez más a Cristo.

blocks.en: VII. The Danger of Neglecting Follow-Up
blocks.es_reference: VII. El Peligro de Descuidar el Seguimiento

blocks.en: When follow-up is neglected, new believers may become discouraged, misunderstandings may develop, and spiritual growth may be hindered. Evangelism without discipleship leads to incomplete ministry. The seed may sprout, but without cultivation it is easily choked or scorched.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando se descuida el seguimiento, los nuevos creyentes pueden desanimarse, pueden desarrollarse malentendidos y el crecimiento espiritual puede ser estorbado. El evangelismo sin discipulado conduce a un ministerio incompleto. La semilla puede brotar, pero sin cultivo es fácilmente ahogada o quemada.

blocks.en: VIII. Reproduction in Evangelism
blocks.es_reference: VIII. La Reproducción en el Evangelismo

blocks.en: Disciples are not only learners—they become witnesses.
blocks.es_reference: Los discípulos no son solo aprendices—se convierten en testigos.

blocks.en: "And the things that you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also." (2 Timothy 2:2, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Y lo que has oído de mí entre muchos testigos, esto encarga a hombres fieles que sean idóneos para enseñar también a otros." (2 Timoteo 2:2, RVG)

blocks.en: A healthy pattern follows a clear sequence: evangelism leads to discipleship, and discipleship leads to reproduction. The disciple who is built up becomes, in turn, one who builds up others.
blocks.es_reference: Un patrón sano sigue una secuencia clara: el evangelismo conduce al discipulado, y el discipulado conduce a la reproducción. El discípulo que es edificado se convierte, a su vez, en alguien que edifica a otros.

blocks.en: IX. Illustration and Application
blocks.es_reference: IX. Ilustración y Aplicación

blocks.en: Consider two believers who each lead someone to Christ. One shares the gospel and moves on, leaving the new believer without guidance. The other invests time, teaches, encourages, and walks alongside the new believer. The difference is not in the moment of profession but in the long-term fruit. Months later, one new convert has drifted; the other is grounded, growing, and beginning to share the gospel himself.
blocks.es_reference: Considere a dos creyentes que cada uno guía a alguien a Cristo. Uno comparte el evangelio y sigue adelante, dejando al nuevo creyente sin guía. El otro invierte tiempo, enseña, anima y camina junto al nuevo creyente. La diferencia no está en el momento de la profesión, sino en el fruto a largo plazo. Meses después, un converso se ha desviado; el otro está cimentado, creciendo y comenzando a compartir el evangelio él mismo.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: Evangelism is the beginning, not the end. True faith leads to discipleship, growth, and reproduction. The believer must not only proclaim the gospel, but also participate in the ongoing development of new believers, "teaching them to observe all things" that Christ has commanded.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo es el comienzo, no el fin. La verdadera fe conduce al discipulado, el crecimiento y la reproducción. El creyente no solo debe proclamar el evangelio, sino también participar en el desarrollo continuo de los nuevos creyentes, "enseñándoles que guarden todas las cosas" que Cristo ha mandado.

sa.prompt: Explain why evangelism should be understood as the beginning of discipleship rather than its completion.
sa.model: Evangelism should be understood as the beginning of discipleship rather than its completion because the new birth is a starting point, not a finish line. When someone trusts Christ, a lifelong process of growth begins. Treating conversion as the end leaves new believers untaught and vulnerable; treating it as the beginning leads us to nurture, teach, and ground them. The Great Commission itself joins making disciples with teaching them to obey, showing evangelism opens the door to a journey of growth.

sa.prompt: Using Matthew 28:19–20, explain the difference between making converts and making disciples.
sa.model: Matthew 28:19–20 commands making disciples, baptizing, and teaching them to obey all Christ commanded. The difference between making converts and making disciples is that a convert has merely professed faith, while a disciple is being taught, grounded, and shaped into obedient followership. Making converts stops at the decision; making disciples continues through teaching and obedience. The commission is not fulfilled by counting decisions but by developing obedient followers of Christ.

sa.prompt: According to Matthew 7:21, why is not every profession of faith evidence of genuine conversion, and how does follow-up help?
sa.model: Matthew 7:21 warns that not everyone who says 'Lord, Lord' will enter the kingdom, so not every profession of faith is evidence of genuine conversion. Some make a verbal decision without real repentance and faith. Follow-up helps by revealing whether the profession bears fruit: as the new believer is taught and observed over time, genuine faith shows itself in growth and obedience, while a false profession often fades. Follow-up protects against false assurance and confirms true conversion.

sa.prompt: Explain why immediate follow-up is important, using the example of the early church in Acts 2:42.
sa.model: Immediate follow-up is important because new believers are most vulnerable right after conversion and need grounding before doubts, old habits, or opposition pull them back. Acts 2:42 shows the early church's pattern: the new converts continued steadfastly in the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayer — right away. The church surrounded them at once with instruction and community. Delayed follow-up risks losing the new believer; immediate care establishes him while the soil is soft.

sa.prompt: Name several foundational truths a new believer must be taught, and explain why grounding matters (1 Peter 2:2).
sa.model: A new believer must be taught foundational truths such as assurance of salvation, the authority of Scripture, the habit of prayer, the importance of the local church, and how to grow in obedience. 1 Peter 2:2 says that as newborn babies they should desire the pure milk of the word that they may grow. Grounding matters because an untaught believer remains weak and easily shaken; foundational truth gives him stability, assurance, and the means to keep growing into maturity.

sa.prompt: Describe the role of the local church in discipleship, using Acts 2:47. Why should discipleship not occur in isolation?
sa.model: Acts 2:47 shows the Lord adding to the church those who were being saved — new believers were joined to the local body. The local church's role in discipleship is to provide teaching, fellowship, accountability, and the means of grace that nurture growth. Discipleship should not occur in isolation because Christians grow through one another: alone, a believer lacks the encouragement, correction, and example the body supplies. God designed maturity to happen within the community of His people, not apart from it.

sa.prompt: Explain how spiritual growth happens (2 Peter 3:18) and why it is described as gradual but intentional.
sa.model: 2 Peter 3:18 calls believers to grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. Spiritual growth is gradual but intentional: gradual because maturity develops over time like a child growing up, not all at once; intentional because it does not happen automatically but through deliberate means — reading the word, prayer, fellowship, and obedience. The believer must pursue growth purposefully while accepting that it unfolds slowly, trusting God to mature him step by step.

sa.prompt: Describe the dangers of neglecting follow-up, and explain why evangelism without discipleship is incomplete ministry.
sa.model: Neglecting follow-up is dangerous because new believers left untaught can drift back into old patterns, fall under discouragement or false teaching, and never grow — some abandoning the faith they professed. Evangelism without discipleship is incomplete ministry because the Great Commission commands not only making converts but teaching them to obey. To win someone and then abandon him is like delivering a baby and walking away; the work is only half done until the new believer is grounded and growing.

sa.prompt: Using 2 Timothy 2:2, explain the pattern of reproduction: evangelism, discipleship, and reproduction.
sa.model: 2 Timothy 2:2 says to commit what you have heard to faithful men who will be able to teach others also. This reveals the pattern of reproduction: evangelism wins a person, discipleship grounds and matures him, and reproduction means he in turn wins and disciples others. The goal is not to gather converts who only receive, but to make disciples who become disciple-makers. Each generation teaches the next, so that the gospel multiplies through faithful believers passing it on.

sa.prompt: Synthesize the unit: explain the believer's responsibility not only to proclaim the gospel but to develop new believers.
sa.model: The believer's responsibility is not only to proclaim the gospel but to develop new believers into mature disciples. Evangelism begins the work; discipleship completes it. This means following up immediately, teaching foundational truths, bringing the new believer into the local church, nurturing gradual growth, and aiming for reproduction so he disciples others. The Great Commission joins proclamation and development: we are called to make disciples, not merely converts, so that those we win grow up and pass on the faith.
